item.research_question: What is the specific role of each cation in the high-entropy oxide Mg0.2Co0.2Ni0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2O during electrochemical cycling, and how does their synergy explain the 'cocktail effect' and structural reversibility in conversion-type reactions?
item.processing_route: Nebulized spray pyrolysis (NSP) at 1150 °C using a mist speed of 40 mL/h and N2 carrier gas; electrode preparation involved mixing with Super C65 and PVDF (7:2:1 ratio) on copper foil, dried at 80 °C.
item.test_conditions: Coin-type half-cells with Li foil counter/reference, 1 M LiPF6 in EC/EMC electrolyte, cycled between 0.01 V and 3.0 V at 50 mA/g; characterized via XAS, S/TEM, 4D-STEM, electron tomography, and in-situ TEM-STM conductivity measurements.
key_findings: Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn are reduced to metallic states during the first discharge, forming a CoNiCu alloy and LiZn phase.
Upon charging, Ni and Cu remain metallic, while Zn is almost fully reoxidized to the 2+ state and a large fraction of Co reoxidizes.
The discharged sample consists of a metallic phase (Co, Ni, Cu) and an oxide phase (O, Mg, Li) with Zn forming a separate LiZn nanophase.
The metallic phase forms a 3D dendritic network at grain boundaries and inside grains, providing a continuous electron transport path.
The oxide phase (Mg-dominated) is semi-coherent with the metallic phase and accommodates Li+ ions.
The charged particle exhibits significantly higher electrical conductivity (0.1 µA at 15 V) compared to the insulating as-prepared sample.
The structural features (phase separation and network) are maintained after 5 cycles, confirming high reversibility.
The theoretical capacity for the first discharge is 687 mAh/g (611 mAh/g from CoNiCu + 76 mAh/g from LiZn).
item.mechanism: The synergy arises from distinct cation roles: (i) Zn and Co provide electrochemical capacity; (ii) Mg2+ is electrochemically inert and stabilizes the oxide nanophase that accommodates Li+; (iii) Cu and Ni remain metallic to form a 3D conductive backbone. This self-assembled nanostructure bypasses the need for pre-nanostructuring, mechanically stabilizes the particle, and ensures fast reaction kinetics by reducing the reaction path to the nanometer level.
item.limitations: The initial HEO structure cannot be restored during the first charge cycle because the high configurational entropy required for the single-phase solid solution is only effective at the synthesis temperature (>877 °C) and is insufficient to stabilize the structure at room temperature during conversion reactions. Additionally, the exact presence of nano/sub-nanometer scale Li2O aggregates cannot be ruled out due to detection limits.
item.future_work: The findings can help to design new conversion-type materials for the application as battery electrodes by utilizing elemental diversity to optimize multi-cation electrode materials.
quotes: The more electronegative elements form an electrochemically inert 3-dimensional metallic nano-network enabling electron transport.
The electrochemical inactive cation stabilizes an oxide nanophase, which is semi-coherent with the metallic phase and accommodates Li+ ions.

This self-assembled nanostructure enables stable cycling of micron-sized particles, which bypasses the need for nanoscale pre-modification required for conventional metal oxides in battery applications.
